metadata.title: Scroll Community Grants
metadata.description:
Scroll DAO Community Council introduces the Community Grants Program. This is an effort to support communities worldwide with their community activations. The focus of these activations alongside Scroll should remain in allowing your audience to explore the Scroll ecosystem, its products, assets, or programs. 

**Evaluation Period:** On a rolling basis, 7 days after submission

**Who can apply for support?**
Community organizers from all over the world are welcome to apply. Whether you’ve been hosting local meetups, organizing a university club, running workshops for builders, or anything of a similar nature, we want to hear from you! 

**Are there any compliance requirements for applicants?**
For grants above $2,000, KYC/KYB verification will be required. All applicants will also be asked to sign standard AML statements through the application form.

**What can apply for support?**
Funds can be used to cover the cost of a space, snacks, beverages, and even swag in some cases. We encourage you to focus on items that are crucial to make your activation a success.

**How much funding is available per activation?**
The amount awarded will vary depending on size, scale of the activity, region, but there is a maximum cap of $10,000 USD. Preference towards applicants that propose a reasonable budget. We encourage smaller grassroots activations, rather than lavish gatherings.

**Can I apply for a virtual event?**
Yes, it can! We are accepting applications for in-person events, virtual, or hybrid.

**When is the deadline for the activity to take place?**
The activity must happen before January 31st, 2026.

**Do we need to provide any post-event deliverables?**
Yes, but nothing fancy. Any photos, videos, or social media posts that we can amplify would be great. Plus a brief recap on the Governance Forum to share your updates with the rest of our community.

**Can we collaborate with other local communities or sponsors?**
Yes! We encourage collaborations across different groups.

**When is the deadline for applications?**
Applications should be submitted by December 19th, 2025 at 11:59 UTC

**Any other questions?**
Reach out to community@scroll.io and we will be happy to answer any other questions you may have.

metadata.title: Prezenti Anchor Pool
metadata.description:
# Season 2: Anchor Open Round [2026]

**STATUS: OPEN**

## Current Round

This round is open 25th February 2026 - 30th June 2026 [$220,000 USDm available]

## Timeline

- This round is open 25th February 2026 - 30th June 2026
- Inform outcome to applicants: Within 2-4 weeks of submission, offered on a rolling basis
- Close out / end of grants: 4 months after contract signatory

## Anchor Mission and Fund Allocation

In alignment with Season 2's focus on sustainable ecosystem growth, Prezenti plans to explicitly support applications that generate revenue for the chain, whether through transaction fees, sequencer revenue contribution, or other mechanisms. This extends beyond the existing intent framework to teams building durable, revenue-positive infrastructure.

### The Revenue Concentration Reality

Analysis of mature L2 ecosystems reveals a consistent pattern: a small number of high-throughput, revenue-generating applications drive the overwhelming majority of sustainable chain economics. On leading L2s, it's common for a single application category — whether DEXs, prediction markets, or payments infrastructure — to account for 40–60% of total ecosystem revenue. Networks that attract these anchor applications early compound their advantage through liquidity effects, user retention, and sustainable fee generation. The key differentiator is no longer technical. Arguably it has never been: it's distribution.

## Eligibility & Focus

**What we're looking for:**

- Verifiable evidence of real usage (transactions, users, revenue)
- Clear path to generating meaningful transaction volume on Celo
- Product-market fit demonstrated elsewhere, or credible pilot results within MiniPay
- Teams slightly below Stage 2 funding thresholds may be considered where a proven track record and substantial evidence demonstrate imminent viability

| Stage | Profile | Est. Daily TXs | Grant size |
|-------|---------|----------------|------------|
| Stage 1 | — | >5k daily tx's | — |
| Stage 2 | Valora apps, Mini apps | 10K – 100K | $25k est |
| Stage 3 | Seed-stage or scaled products with traction | 100k–500k | $50k est |
| Stage 4 | Mature ecosystem apps | 500k+ | Case-by-case |

- **Must** demonstrate 10k–100k daily transactions on Celo mainnet [if you cannot demonstrate these daily tx's then you should be able to demonstrate a good level of sustained transactions over a period of time]
- We are ideally looking for a sustained daily average over 5,000 tx
- Projects should be deployed, open to the public, and open source or published

## Not Eligible

- Ongoing salaries, pure marketing spend, events, liquidity provision, token listings, or general VC investment
- Applications gaming transaction counts without generating underlying value, e.g. spamming micro USDT transfers to addresses with little previous history
- Projects without verifiable traction or credible usage evidence
- Teams that cannot articulate how they contribute to transaction growth or TVL

## General Information

- One-off grant cUSD to all successful applicants
- Payments will be split 20% at project onset, and 80% after agreed delivery
- For unsuccessful applications there will be some feedback
- Applicants will be KYC'ed and sign a contract with Prezenti

## Evaluation Rubric

The Prezenti review team will use the rubric below to help guide and grade proposals. To arrive at a final decision, Prezenti will evaluate each proposal and come to a consensus through an internal vote.

| Criterion | Score | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Alignment | 0: No clear alignment / 1: Partial alignment with no notable gaps | — |
| Open Source Commitment | 0: No / 1: Yes / Partial | Comment |
| Demo Quality | 0: No demo / 1: Yes / Explains concept | — |
| Team Assessment | 0: Can't assess / bad / 1: Strong team | — |
| Metrics / KPIs | 0: Not good / 1: Somewhat good / good | — |
| Correctly specified their appropriate stage? | 0: No / 1: Yes | — |
| Clear understanding of the actual demand for this product | 0: Not clear, no real understanding demonstrated / 1: Somewhat good / good | — |
| Do they have a clear financial plan for sustainable growth? | 0: No / 1: Yes / Partial | — |
| Discretionary factor | -1 / 0 / 1 | Comment |

Welcome to Devlynix Buildathon 1.0, an asynchronous, weekend-long mini-hackathon designed specifically to help you transition from watching tutorials to building practical, real-world projects.

This hackathon focuses on the "Idea-to-MVP Sprint" model. We aren't looking for perfect code; we are looking for strong problem-solving, clean design, and a solid technical approach.

# **⚠️ IMPORTANT: MANDATORY STEP**

All official announcements, squad formations, and shortlisting results will be shared EXCLUSIVELY on our WhatsApp handles. Joining both is mandatory for participation.

👉 Join our WhatsApp Channel: https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VbCzGzaJpe8chzjL0w1F
👉 Join our Community Group: https://chat.whatsapp.com/EJrdn43jObx00BKnp444Rj

# ​📅 **Event Overview**

**Format:** 48-Hour Asynchronous Online Hackathon
**Team Size**: 1 to 4 Members per Squad
**Goal:** Build a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) addressing specific community tech challenges.

# 🛠️ The Challenge: Choose Your Problem Statement
Squads must select one of the following real-world challenges to solve. Your goal is to build a functional MVP with a clean User Interface.

> **1. The Developer Proof-of-Work Platform 🚀**
Many developers build great projects but lose them in scattered GitHub repositories. Build a centralized showcase directory where developers can host their deployed projects, tag their tech stack, and attach demo videos. Include filtering options (e.g., MERN, Web3, AI) for easy discovery.

>**2. The "Execution-First" Accountability Tracker 🔥**
Students often get stuck in "tutorial hell." Build a web dashboard that tracks a user's daily or weekly "build streak" based on actual project execution. The app should prompt users with "What did you code today?", visualize their consistency, and reward them with milestones.

>**3. The Skill-Based Teammate Matchmaker 🤝**
Finding the right teammates for hackathons or side projects is a major hurdle. Design a user-directory system where individuals can create profiles highlighting their specific skills (e.g., UI/UX, React, AI) and proficiency levels. Implement a search and filter mechanism to connect users.

> **4. The Crowdsourced Learning Vault 📚**
The internet is flooded with scattered resources. Build an organized, community-driven resource hub where users can submit and categorize high-quality links, tools, and guides. Include an upvote/downvote system so the best resources naturally rise to the top.

>**5. The Micro-Event & Submission Portal 🎯**
Small tech communities struggle to manage asynchronous events through chaotic group chats. Create a streamlined event dashboard displaying hackathon details, rules, and deadlines. It must feature a dedicated submission portal where teams can upload their final deliverables.

# 🎯 What You Need to Submit (The Deliverables)
To successfully complete the hackathon, your squad must submit the following three items:

 > **1. The Website MVP (Minimum Viable Product)**

**Build What You Can:** If you are a beginner, building just a clean, functional frontend MVP is completely fine. If you have the skills, you are highly encouraged to build the full-stack version (Frontend + Backend/Database)!

> **2. The Pitch Video (Max 10 Minutes)**

This is your final presentation! Record your screen and your voice.
**How to do it:** Walk us through your PPT first, and then give a live demo of your Website MVP.
**The Vibe:** Be confident! Explain your thought process, why you designed the UI a certain way, and how the code logic works.

# 📅 Buildathon 1.0: Official Timeline
**Phase 1: Registration & Concept Submission**
Date: 4th May
Duration: 24 Hours
Task: Register your team on Devfolio and start working on any problem statement given above.

**Phase 2: The 48-Hour Build Sprint**
Task: Start coding your MVP (Minimum Viable Product). This is the main development phase where you build your frontend/full-stack solution.
Submission: Keep your Deployed Website Link.

**Phase 3: Final Submission & Video Pitch**
Final Deliverables: 
1. Deployed Website Link. (In Project Links)
2. GitHub Repo URL. (In Project Links)
3. Final Video Demo (Max 10 Minutes):(YouTube link)

Important: The Devfolio submission portal will automatically close at 11:59 PM on 6th May.

**📅 Important Instructions for Participants:**

Strict Deadlines: Submissions after the round deadline will lead to automatic disqualification.

Communication: All shortlisting announcements will be made via the official Devlynix WhatsApp group and Devfolio notifications.

# 📊 Evaluation Criteria
Judges will evaluate your submissions out of 100 Points based on these 4 pillars:

**Problem-Solution Fit (25 Points):** How practical and realistic is your solution?
**UI/UX & Design (25 Points):** Is the layout user-friendly, clean, and adhering to the 'Silent Coder' aesthetic?
**Technical Logic (25 Points):** How functional is the code, or how clearly is the technical architecture defined?
**The Final Pitch (25 Points):** How well was the product explained and demonstrated in the video?

*Get ready to build. Good luck, Squads! Let's build something awesome. 🛠️🔥*

metadata.title: RFP: Reboot the Gitcoin Community for the 3.3 Era
metadata.description:
A vendor solicitation posted to the Gitcoin DAO governance forum for the work of rebuilding the DAO's community around its 3.3 relaunch. It is split into three workstreams, and a bidder may bid on one of them or on all three:

1. Delegate recruitment — finding and onboarding credible GTC delegates and getting tokens delegated to them.
2. Community re-onboarding — bringing lapsed and new contributors back in, with the education and documentation that requires.
3. A launch campaign plan for the Q4 2026 / Q1 2027 window.

No budget envelope is published: bidders name their own price and justify it. Proposals are read on a rolling basis, with the first review noted for 1 June 2026 and the engagement window running from June 2026 into Q1 2027. The solicitation is posted as a draft under governance discussion, so its terms may still change. Proposals are directed to the contact named in the posting, with a cross-post to the forum thread so the discussion stays public.

metadata.title: Rocket Pool GMC Grants — Round 40
metadata.description:
Monthly rolling grants funded from Rocket Pool's RPL treasury for community-proposed work the applicant will personally carry out, judged on how much it grows node operation, rETH usage, or protocol and community quality of life. Round 40 covers the August 7 - September 7, 2026 cycle.

The round's call for applications states an application period of August 7 to September 7, 2026, a scoring deadline of September 22, and an award announcement on September 27. The Grants and Marketing Committee treasury receives 16,265.35 RPL every 28 days under RPIP-81, shared across the grants, bounty, and retrospective tracks; the treasury was reported at roughly $29.7k in the August 2026 report, so no single per-grant figure is published.
metadata.shortDescription: Monthly RPL-funded grants for community work that grows Rocket Pool node operation and rETH usage; Round 40 closes September 7, 2026.

metadata.title: Mantle EcoFund
metadata.description:
Rolling ecosystem-support fund for early-stage projects seeking a long-term partnership with Mantle Network. Provides deal-structuring and fundraising help, co-promotion, enhanced delegated voting rights, exchange-listing support, and direct access to the Mantle Growth team rather than a fixed grant check.

The live EcoFund page lists 40+ portfolio companies tagged 'Live' spanning DeFi, gaming, Bitcoin infrastructure and AI, and names ecofund@mantle.xyz as the contact for interested projects; no closing date is shown and no funding figure is disclosed. Intake is that email contact rather than a public form, and the program resembles an investment and partnership vehicle more than a traditional grant.
metadata.shortDescription: Rolling ecosystem-support fund for early-stage projects partnering with Mantle Network; intake is by email to the address on the program page.

metadata.title: ArbiFuel (Gas Fee Sponsorship Program)
metadata.description:
Gas-fee sponsorship for early-stage teams building simplified-UX apps, wallets, stablecoin products, or payment applications on Arbitrum, covering onboarding costs through ERC-20 paymasters so users do not need ETH for gas.

The Arbitrum Foundation's grants index lists ArbiFuel as Active with a live 'Apply now' button. Terms are up to 1,000,000 sponsored transactions in a team's first year, capped at $10,000 in credits per team — sponsorship credit rather than a cash grant, which is why no cash grant size is recorded here.
metadata.shortDescription: Gas-fee sponsorship on Arbitrum: up to 1,000,000 sponsored transactions in a team's first year, capped at $10,000 in credits.

An ArbitrumDAO initiative designed to empower builders of gaming projects and infrastructure within the Arbitrum ecosystem. Connect with the AGV team to explore grants, funding opportunities, tools, and collaboration possibilities.
